title: Iran fires ballistic missiles at Israel after killings of Nasrallah and Haniyeh
body:
On the evening of 1 October 2024 Iran fired nearly 200 projectiles at Israel. The Israeli military put the figure at 180 ballistic missiles. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said the attack responded to Israeli strikes in Gaza and Lebanon and to the killings of Hezbollah leader Hassan Nasrallah and IRGC commander Abbas Nilforoushan in Beirut, and of Hamas leader Ismail Haniyeh in Tehran in July.

The IRGC first described the targets as vital military and security sites and then said it aimed at three military bases in the Tel Aviv area. Iranian state media said Fatah hypersonic ballistic missiles were used for the first time. Israel and the United States said their forces shot down most of the missiles, with US destroyers joining Israeli air defences, and Israel reported isolated impacts in central and southern Israel. The IRGC claimed that 90 percent of projectiles hit their targets.

Israel's emergency service reported two people injured by shrapnel in the Tel Aviv area, and US National Security Adviser Jake Sullivan said no deaths were reported in Israel. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Iran had "made a big mistake" and "will pay for it." Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said Iran did not seek war, UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres called for a ceasefire, and the US pledged "ironclad" support for Israel. Israel's retaliation came on 26 October 2024.
